title: Table
summary: Complete server-backed collection view with search, filters, table preferences, row and bulk actions, and pagination.

template.description: Template variant name for SfBaseElement external templates.

root-class.description: Classes added to the root element the component draws.

root-style.description: Inline style declarations set on the root element the component draws, custom properties included.

creatable.description: The create button and its menu of kinds, inside actions. A data view turns it off for a host on port 1.10.0 that does not announce create-record.

filter-templates.description: The button that saves the filter as a template. A data view turns it off when the host keeps no saved views.

settings-menu.description: The gear in the head of the settings column, which opens the column settings. Off, the column still carries each row's menu. A data view turns it off for a host on port 1.10.0 that does not announce personal-column-settings.

context-menu-columns.description: How many columns the settings menu splits its items into. One until a host asks for more: the read was bare for the whole life of this input, so neither its declared default nor a value a host passed ever reached the menu.

remember-widths.description: Remember the column widths as a view preference (SF.Preferences, under preferences-key or table-settings-key) for a table no host keeps settings for; a double click on a column's edge forgets that column's width.

table-settings-key.description: Which stored settings this table uses. Empty means the element's own id, and then its instance id, so each table on a page keeps its own. A real default here would make every table share one key and overwrite the others.

toolbar.description: Show the built-in toolbar; a composite can provide its own toolbar slot.

pin-column-label.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the control that pins a column.

unpin-column-label.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the control that unpins a column.

column-move-label.description: Accessible name of the handle that moves a column in the settings list; the column label is appended to it.

column-search-placeholder.description: Placeholder and accessible name of the search field above the column settings list.

column-search-empty-text.description: Shown in place of the column settings list when the search matches no field.

vertical-scroll.description: Whether the table scrolls within itself or lets the page scroll. Declared as a string with two values; the manifest previously said boolean true, which was wrong in both the type and the default.

filter-apply-text.description: Label of the filter window’s commit button; the number of conditions a press would change is appended to it while a draft is pending.

layout.description: How the records are drawn: a table, a compact list of records, or auto -- a table while the table's container is at least list-below pixels wide, the list below that. sf-view asks for auto on a page's list. With layout-switch, the person's choice comes first.

layout-switch.description: A list/table switch (sf-segmented, two icons) in the toolbar before Create (owner decision C31). The choice is the person's: kept with the table's preferences (preferences-key, table-settings-key or remember-widths, else for the page) and in the settings of a saved view; with it, layout table reads as auto. Below list-below there is only the list and no switch.

list-below.description: The container width, in pixels, below which layout auto draws the compact list.

list-fields.description: How many fields a record shows under its title in the compact list, chosen by the columns' priority.

quick-actions.description: The row actions a list row shows as icon buttons, always visible: their ids, comma-separated, at most three (owner decision C31). The rest stay in the row menu, which in the list is «more» (more_horiz) instead of the menu icon; on a narrow list (below 37.5rem) the quick ones fold into it too. An action without an icon is a text button.

row-open.description: What a press on a row opens: title, the title link alone (and a double click, Enter); row, a press anywhere in the row but its controls opens the record through the same view intent (sf-view-table-apply view), in the table and in the list (owner decision C31).

size.description: The step of the size ladder the table's controls and rows take: 1, or the dense 1/2 -- 32px controls, 14/20 text, rows of the step's height. A size of 1 written on an element the table draws becomes the table's.

preferences-key.description: The key this table's arrangement -- order, visibility, pinning, widths -- is kept under as a view preference (SF.Preferences, sf-table/<key>); a data view passes its own. Without it table-settings-key is used, and without either nothing is kept.

row-actions-visible.description: Where a row's action buttons are drawn: in the row under the pointer, with the focus or current (hover, the default), or in every row (always).

drag-rows.description: Rows may be dragged out of the list as records (application/x-sf-records+json): the row's record, or every selected record when it is one of them.

row-reorder.description: Rows can be put in another order by dragging them inside the list; a drop emits sf-table-rows-reorder {ids, before, order}. A data view sets it when the host offers row-reorder.

inline-edit.description: A boolean cell the record names in `editable` is a checkbox; pressing it emits sf-table-cell-set {id, key, value, revision} and the cell waits for the host. A data view sets it when the host offers inline-edit.

current.description: The id of the row the page has open: that row carries aria-current and data-current. Writing it marks the row; it does not focus it and sends no event (component.json settings.current).

aria-label.description: The table's accessible name. Read it from the props context and never from the element: `aria-label` is reflected by the platform, so element.ariaLabel returns null with no attribute set and shadows what the component resolves. Whether an English default belongs in a family whose other fourteen text inputs default to Russian is the owner's open question about the Framework's default language.

selection.description: the marked rows' ids, in row order

addRows.summary: Append another backend page for show-more mode.

applyQueryResult.summary: Apply rows answering the newest pending context query. Returns false and changes nothing for a stale, repeated or unknown sequence.

clearSelection.summary: Clear the explicit selection of this instance; emits the selection port once when it changes.

requestActionIntent.summary: Emit a typed row or bulk action request; the host owns execution and authorization. Invalid arguments throw TypeError before emission.

requestCreateIntent.summary: Emit sf-table-create-intent for the main button (null) or a declared create item id.

requestRetry.summary: Emit a retry intent after a failed data request.

setSort.summary: Show the host's current sort on the headers without emitting an event; (null, null) clears it.

toggleTreeRow.summary: Say that a tree row was opened or closed (sf-table-tree-toggle).

requestTreeMore.summary: Ask for the next page of a tree level (sf-table-tree-more).

setLayout.summary: Choose the list or the table for this person, as the layout switch does: kept with the table's preferences and drawn. Refused for another value; unchanged when it is the choice already.

getActiveFilterFieldKeys.summary: Which filter fields the filter is showing, in the host's field order.

getFilterPayload.summary: Read the current filter draft for host-side query validation.

getInstanceId.summary: Identity of this instance: the author's id when there is one, an own counter otherwise. Ids, the settings key fallback and the portal derive from it.

getQueryContext.summary: Read the immutable context last received through the context input port, or null.

getSelectedRecordIds.summary: Read the typed record identities selected in this table result, without DOM parsing.

getSort.summary: Read the sort shown on the headers.

getToolbarActions.summary: The toolbar actions as declared, copied.

requestContextQuery.summary: Internal to the context port: emit sf-table-query-intent for the current context with a new pending sequence.

setActiveFilterFields.summary: Show exactly these filter fields in the selected filter template. Used when a saved view is opened: settings.filter_fields names the fields it was showing.

setBulkActions.summary: Register labeled opaque actions for the current selection. Empty selection disables their controls.

setCreateItems.summary: Set the create split-button menu items ({id, name} only). Without items the create button has no arrow.

setDataState.summary: Switch between automatic, loading, populated, empty and error presentation states.

setFilterFields.summary: Register backend-allowlisted filter fields and controls.

setRows.summary: Replace the current backend result rows.

setTableData.summary: Patch columns, rows or related table state supplied by the host.

setTableSettings.summary: Apply a column-preference delta without emitting a save request.

setToolbarActions.summary: Declare the view's own actions for the toolbar menu: {id, label, icon?, href?}. An href must name this same site. Without actions the control is not rendered.

sfPortInput.summary: Composition input port entry used by sf-composition-scope. Accepts only the declared context port with record-ids.v1; invalid ports or values throw TypeError before any state change.

isTree.summary: Whether the rows are a tree: some row carries __tree, written by the data view from the host's levels.

treeColumnKey.summary: The column a tree hangs from: the title column, or the first data column.

sf-view-table-select.summary: The marked rows changed, vocabulary §5 select {ids}: once per change of the explicit selection, clearing included. The old name sf-port-output follows once with its old detail until 2026-12-01 (aliases.json).

sf-view-table-apply.summary: A row's or the selection's action, vocabulary §5 apply: {action, scope: entry | selection, ids, revisions}. The host decides; emission is not success. The old name sf-table-action-intent follows once with its old detail until 2026-12-01 (aliases.json).

sf-view-table-save.summary: The person's column settings, vocabulary §5 save {kind: columns, reason, columnSettings, tableSettingsKey}. The old name sf-table-column-settings-change follows once with its old detail until 2026-12-01 (aliases.json).

columnSettings.description: The column settings now in force (order, widths, pinned, hidden).

sf-view-table-column-settings-reset.summary: The person asked for the default columns back. The table drops its own stored arrangement and names no defaults: the host (or a data view) resets the person's layer and answers with its defaults.

target.description: The layer to reset. The table only resets the person's own layer.

tableSettingsKey.description: The table's settings key, or null when it has none.

sf-view-table-create.summary: The create button or one of its kinds, vocabulary §5 create {item}. The old name sf-table-create-intent follows once with its old detail until 2026-12-01 (aliases.json).

sf-view-table-filter-change.summary: Request a host-side query after the active filter changes: Apply in the filter window, a chip removed, or the filter cleared. A data view turns it into query.change with filters from values. The detail is the table's getFilterPayload(): the selected template's own data fields spread first, then these four.

templateKey.description: The selected template's key, or an empty string.

templateLabel.description: The selected template's label, or an empty string.

values.description: The filter values now in force, keyed by filter field.

tags.description: The active filter chips, keyed by filter field.

sf-view-table-query.summary: A context query of the composition input port, vocabulary §5.1 query {reason, context, sequence}. The old name sf-table-query-intent follows once with its old detail until 2026-12-01 (aliases.json).

sf-view-table-refresh.summary: The retry button of a failed list, vocabulary §5 refresh. The old name sf-table-retry follows once with its old detail until 2026-12-01 (aliases.json).

sf-view-table-search-change.summary: Request a host-side query after the debounced search value changes.

sf-view-table-sort-change.summary: The user activated a sortable header. Direction cycles asc, desc, null (unsorted). Intent only: the table marks the header but does not reorder rows; the host reorders or reloads.

sf-view-table-template-delete.summary: The user deleted saved templates on the Templates tab and pressed Apply. Intent only: the host removes the saved view. One event per deleted template.

sf-view-table-template-save.summary: Request persistence of one or more filter templates (order, pin, delete, default, selected flags or data): detail {templates}, one entry or several. Loading a saved view is reported by sf-table-template-select.

templates.description: The saved templates: one when a template is saved from the form, several when Apply on the Templates tab changed several (order, pin, default, selected).

key.description: The template's key; a new template gets filter_template_<n>.

label.description: The name the person gave it.

selected.description: Whether it is the applied template.

data.description: The filter draft it keeps: the form values, `values` and `tags`.

filter_fields.description: The filter fields it was showing, so opening it shows them again.

settings.description: Passed through by the port as it is.

sf-view-table-template-select.summary: The user applied a different saved template on the Templates tab. Intent only: the host loads that saved view.

sf-view-table-toolbar-action.summary: The user chose one of the view's own actions from the toolbar menu. Intent only, and cancelable: the component follows an item's same-site href unless the host takes the navigation over with preventDefault.

sf-view-table-expand.summary: A tree row opened or closed, vocabulary §5 expand {id, expanded}. The old name sf-table-tree-toggle follows once with its old detail until 2026-12-01 (aliases.json).

sf-view-table-load-more.summary: The next page of a tree level, vocabulary §5 load-more {direction: after, parent, cursor}. The old name sf-table-tree-more follows once with its old detail until 2026-12-01 (aliases.json).

sf-view-table-rows-drag.summary: Rows began to be dragged out of a list with drag-rows, for a drop target such as a tree; the same {ids, source} rides in the drag data as application/x-sf-records+json.

ids.description: The ids dragged: every selected id when the dragged row is selected, otherwise that row's id alone.

source.description: Where the rows come from: the table's preferences-key, table-settings-key or id, or null.

sf-view-table-move.summary: Rows put in another order, vocabulary §5 move {ids, before, order}. The old name sf-table-rows-reorder follows once with its old detail until 2026-12-01 (aliases.json).

sf-view-table-cell-set.summary: A checkable cell was pressed: the record, the field, the new value and the record's revision.

sf-view-table-window.summary: The rows drawn of a long list changed (standard 1.3.8 §18.4): {first, last}, row indexes in the list.

sf-view-table-layout-change.summary: The person chose the list or the table with the layout switch (or set-layout was called); the choice is already kept. sf-view keeps it with the view.

sf-port-output.summary: Composition port output. The table emits port selection (record-ids.v1) once per change of its explicit selection, including clearing; a common sf-composition-scope routes it.

sf-table-action-intent.summary: Request one host-resolved row or bulk operation. Event source is the owning table instance; emission is not operation success.

sf-table-column-settings-change.summary: Request persistence of a column preference delta after resize, reorder or visibility changes.

sf-table-create-intent.summary: The user pressed the create button (item null) or chose an item from its menu (item id). Intent only: the host opens its create form.

sf-table-query-intent.summary: Request a host-side query after the context input port changed. The host resolves the relation and access, then answers with applyQueryResult(sequence, rows); older sequences are ignored.

sf-table-retry.summary: Request another host-side load after the error state.

sf-table-tree-toggle.summary: The person opened or closed a tree row. The data view answers it; the table only says which row and whether it was open.

sf-table-tree-more.summary: The person asked for the next page of one tree level.

sf-table-rows-reorder.summary: Rows were dragged into another order inside the list: the ids that moved, the row they now stand before (null: the end) and the whole order shown.

columnSettings.description: The person's column arrangement, per column key: visible (boolean), width (CSS length), order (number), pinned (start or end). Merged onto the host's column settings, so a column it does not name keeps the host's.

widths.description: Column widths the person dragged, per column key, as "<N>px". Kept also without a preferences-key when the table has remember-widths (then under the table's own key).

view.description: The table's look: density (compact, normal, spacious), stripes, lines, singleLine, stickyHead. Under sf-table/* it is the person's look for every table, read under this table's own.

sort.description: The sort the person chose: [{key, direction}]. Written and read by the data view the table is in, so the first query comes in this order.

pageSize.description: The page size the person chose. Written and read by the data view, so the first query asks for it.

integration_examples.event_bridge: Normalize SF runtime events to Data View intents, validate them in larena/dataview, then return a fresh access-filtered projection.

untrusted_inputs: Reject unknown columns, filters, sorts and action IDs
Treat every row and structured cell as untrusted render data
Never accept record ownership or access flags from the browser

keyboard: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight resize a focused resizable column
accessibility.focus: Every icon-only action and contextual surface has an accessible name. Per-instance overlays stay inside the visual viewport, close on Escape and restore focus to their trigger. Column resize keeps focus on its native button.

changes: Add sf-table-action-intent and requestActionIntent for row, context and bulk operations.
Replace the placeholder View modal with a host-resolved intent; preserve explicit trusted callback overrides.
Selection preserves complete typed IDs; bulk controls use the current-result selection only.
Publish Composition ports: output selection and input context, both record-ids.v1.
Add sf-table-query-intent, applyQueryResult (latest result wins), getQueryContext and clearSelection.
Emit sf-port-output once per explicit selection change; no endpoint, action or query text is emitted.
After remount, a table whose context query was left unanswered requests the same context once with a new sequence.
Add sf-table-create-intent: the create button emits {item: null}; setCreateItems adds an arrow menu whose items emit {item: id}. Without items the arrow is not rendered.
Add sf-table-template-select {key} when Apply on the Templates tab changes the selected template; sf-table-template-save is unchanged.
Columns with sortable: true render a header button with aria-sort and emit sf-table-sort-change {key, direction}; setSort and getSort mirror the host's sort. Rows are never reordered by the table.
Filter fields with filter.optionRenderer 'badge' render options as tonal sf-badge labels coloured by option.color (a badge scheme or a hex colour) with optional option.icon.
The actions column is a system column: not resizable or draggable and no longer frozen into column settings.
Fix: dropping a dragged column no longer duplicates header and body cells; ending a column drag or pointer resize does not sort.

Context menus are anchored to their opener with SF.Position: they flip and shift at the viewport edge and follow the opener on scroll; the filter chip menu opens under the chip instead of the viewport corner.

Filter chips are keyboard operable: each chip label is a button (sf-tag interactive) beside its remove action; Enter or Space opens the chip menu, anchored to the chip, and Escape returns focus to the chip.
The built-in record modal ignores modal:after-close events of nested modals now that modal events bubble.
The manifest moves to smart-component-manifest v2: persistence, ownership, security, accessibility and state use the v2 shape, and adapter, artifacts and readiness are declared.

The five conformance scenarios left the manifest (v2 keeps scenarios in artifacts) and are documented in docs/smart-table-guide.md; studio.fixture.json and studio.scenario.json are the declared artifacts.
No runtime behaviour changes.
Add sf-table-template-delete {key}: deleting a saved template on the Templates tab is its own intent, one event per template; sf-table-template-save keeps reporting the other flags.

Instance isolation: the column resize handles carry per-instance ids (<instance>--column-resizer--<column>), the portal records data-sf-instance, and a table without table-settings-key and without an id falls back to its own instance id instead of the shared key "users".
The region declares its resolved data state: data-state and aria-busy are set on the sf-view-table region, not only on tbody.
Declare the data view as a composition type (smart.view-table): the projection now carries the intents it raises, the data it accepts and where its settings key lives, instead of dropping them.
Add the columns and rows contracts: closed column descriptions and rows with a stable id. They are the data half of the type and the base of the future host port.
No runtime behaviour changes.
Add responsive priority/min_width/sticky projection for declared columns; existing columns keep their previous order and scroll behavior.
Add toolbar=false for a parent composite that supplies a toolbar slot.
Add row-actions: row-actions="false" hides the row action column while actions keeps the create button, for hosts whose row menu is the only entry to a row's actions.

Follows SIMAI Framework release ui-92b4661762ca (standard 1.3.8 display groups A and B): the Loader relations and the composition name the renamed bundles and registry ids (cl-button, cl-icon-button, cl-input, cl-tag, cl-badge; smart.button, smart.icon-button, smart.input, smart.tag, smart.badge).
The empty brick takes heading and the filter's avatars heading, the names sf-empty-state and sf-avatar read since 1.3.8. No public attribute, property or event of sf-view-table changes.

From component.json (standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8): events by the vocabulary's verbs -- sf-table-apply, -select, -save, -create, -query, -refresh, -expand, -load-more, -move -- with the old names as dated aliases until 2026-12-01 (aliases.json); onSearchEnd, onTemplateSave, onFilterUpdate, onColumnSettingsChange and sf-table:column-settings-change follow once each, noted in SF.deprecations.

Many entries (§18.4, simai/ui-pro#2): from 300 rows only the rows in view and a margin are drawn, reported as sf-table-window {first, last}; a plain cell is class markup; one changed row is redrawn in place.
The data state ready, populated its alias; current marks the open row (aria-current); actions answer outcomes.

The windows' portal is watched by the Loader (SF.Loader.watch) and lazy elements are asked for through SF.Loader.ensure; needs core.runtime >= 1.19.0. Nothing to change for a host on a pair from core.runtime 1.19.0 on.

Draws and finds the renamed Framework elements by their new tags (the row and column menus are sf-menu-context (its sf-menu-context-* events), the icon buttons sf-button-icon, the typed cells and editors sf-input-color, sf-input-country, sf-input-date and sf-slider-range; a component type that names a former tag (a host's {type: 'icon-button'}) draws the element under its current tag (canonicalTag of the Smart base)); the rule relations name cl-<new>. Needs the SIMAI Framework pair with the tag renames (core.runtime 1.21.0). No visible change. Nothing to change for a host on that pair; a host that writes the former tags keeps working until 2027-01-01.

The tag is sf-view-table (rename plan R2, naming decision 2026-11-02: sf-[set]-<block>); the folder view-table, the id smart.view-table and the bundle cl-view-table follow it (were table, smart.data-view, cl-table). sf-table stays a dated alias until 2027-01-01: old markup upgrades as this element, the Loader forwards cl-table, and every event fires under its former name as well, with the same detail. Public CSS variables and classes keep their names. Needs the SIMAI Framework pair whose package reference lists the former tag (core.runtime 1.22.0). Nothing to change for a host until 2027-01-01; new markup writes sf-view-table.

A date, date and time or time the host does not format reads in the page's language («2 нояб. 2026 г.», «15 нояб. 2026 г., 10:30», «09:30») instead of as stored; a host's formatFieldValue still wins. An html cell shows its text, not its markup; a cell of several files shows each file's name with its icon. The settings column is left out when it would open nothing (no settings-menu, no row actions, no row-reorder). Nothing to change for a host; a host that relied on stored dates in cells formats them in formatFieldValue.

A filter option drawn as a badge is a tight badge (sf-badge tight, SIMAI Framework sf-badge 1.3.0): it keeps the size's own narrow side room in the dense option list, as a table cell's choice badge does. Needs the pair with sf-badge 1.3.0 (ui-2a671352d67b or newer) to show; on an older pair the attribute is ignored and the badge is as before. Nothing to change for a host.

Its windows -- the filter, field and settings windows and the menus -- are a surface of the document's one layer stack (standard 1.3.8 §19): a press outside closes them through the stack's one listener and Escape through the stack, only while they are the top layer, and they are drawn at the stack's z-index (--sf-z-index-layer and its step) where they read --sf-z-index-9 before; --sf-table-context-menu--z-index still wins. The table bound a document click and keydown of its own: Escape on a window inside a record panel closed the panel too, and a press outside a drawer closed the drawer together with the window over it; now the window closes first. A press on the control that opened a window is still that control's (the gear opens and closes its window). Nothing to change for a host.

sf-view-table-template-save carries {templates}: a list of one template (saved from the form) or several (Apply on the Templates tab), each {key, label, selected, data, settings}, at least one (the decision 'Event detail that is not a flat object', 2026-11-09). The detail used to be the template object itself or an array of them. sf-table-template-save and onTemplateSave keep that former detail through the element's adapter (mode split) until their dates. A host listening to sf-view-table-template-save reads detail.templates; sf-view 1.10.0 does, and still reads a bare template or array until 2027-01-01.

Over SIMAI Framework ui-cb287da78ab1 (core.runtime 1.45.0; the set needs 1.43.0 or newer): the theme roles by their C16 names (--sf-surface-page, --sf-surface-popup, --sf-shadow-popup, --sf-on-surface-popup-variant, --sf-primary-outline, --sf-primary-state-select; the former names are dated aliases of the same values), the icon buttons and buttons ask for appearance ghost (link is its former name, drawn the same). The reference names one args argument per action (standard §4.4); every method the class writes already read the object form beside the fields in order (isActionParameters), and addRows, requestCreateIntent and focusRow also a bare value (x-registry.action-calls). Nothing changes on the page.

The avatar's max-width reads --sf-table-avatar--max-width with the fallback none: a host may still bound the avatar, and a page that sets nothing draws what it drew (the bare reference was unset, so none). The pair range no longer lists a variable bound by the page. Nothing changes on the page.

The list of resources (owner decision C31, 2026-11-09): columns[].list names a column's place in a list row -- status, title, supporting, fact or hidden. With one, a list row is the status dot (its word the tooltip and the accessible text; a stopped resource's word also leads the second line), the title over the supporting fields joined with « · », the facts as sf-badge without labels in columns of one width (8rem; quiet when fine, warning or error when not, the column's label read to a screen reader), then the quick actions and «more». The row is a row of the ladder: 48 at size 1/2, 56 at size 1, 52 on a phone with the title a text step larger. Below 37.5rem only the most worrying fact stays and the quick actions fold into «more». A list without roles is drawn as before.

quick-actions (ids, at most three) draws those row actions as icon buttons in every list row, always visible, with the Framework tooltip; the rest are the «more» menu (more_horiz), which replaces the row menu icon in the list; a narrow list folds the quick ones into it. row-open="row" (the default is title): a press anywhere in a row but its controls opens the record (the view intent, as the title link); the title link is the list row's tab stop, and the arrows, Home and End move from it as from the row (they did nothing in the list before: the focus went only to table rows).

layout-switch: an sf-segmented list/table in the toolbar before Create; the person's choice is kept with the table's preferences (the preference record's layout field) and in a saved view's settings (settings.layout), sent by layout-change and the action set-layout. A list chosen on a wide container keeps the table's toolbar with the switch; below list-below the compact list and its toolbar, no switch.

One row model on the ladder for every table (the look points the owner accepted on 2026-11-09): a body cell's block padding is the rung of two lines of the step's text less those lines and the row's line -- --sf-ui-2--control-height at size 1/2, --sf-ui-3--control-height at size 1 -- and a body row stands on the rung between (block-size --sf-ui-1--control-height at 1/2, --sf-ui-2--control-height at 1). At size 1/2 a one-line row with its box and menu is 40 (it was 45), two lines -- a link with its supporting text or a text wrapped to two lines -- 48 (they were 48 and 53), three lines 68. At size 1 a one-line row with the row menu is 48 (it was 73), two lines 56 (53 and 81 before). The head keeps the step's space around its line, at size 1 from the control ladder (--sf-ui-1--space-y) rather than --sf-space-1: 41, 57 with the box (it was 57 and 73). The published --sf-table-row-*-block-size-* say the same rows (40, 48, 48, 56; head 33, 41). Under compact page density the ladder moves one rung down and the rows with it; a person's view density (data-sf-view-density) keeps its padding.

A column with a list role draws the same value in a table cell: a status as the dot with its word, a fact as its badge (quiet, warning or error, with its tip). The row the person is on (data-current, where the keys and a press leave them) is kept apart from the record the page has open (current, aria-current): the keys no longer move the open record, and list rows carry aria-current as table rows do. Under compact density (data-sf-density="compact", C22, desktop) a table without a size takes the ladder one rung down: 40 with the row's controls, 48 with a supporting line (it was 57 and 61), and the published step-1 box follows on a compact page.

The list's look points (owner, 2026-11-09): the record's title is the surface's text colour (--sf-on-surface), medium weight, underlined while the row is pointed at or the link focused (it was the link colour), and the link draws no ring of its own inside the row's ring. The open record (current, aria-current) has the primary container fill (--sf-primary-container: 12 light, 24 dark); the row the keyboard is on shows the focus ring only. On a phone the row's buttons and «more» are --sf-ui-1--control-height (36; 28 at size 1/2 before). The list has no inline padding and an empty toolbar start takes no gap, so the search field, Create and the rows' fill are on one line (R077). The quick actions still fold below a 37.5rem container.

The controls inside are relative (C22, Larena 2026-11-10): a table without a size writes no size on its toolbar (filter, search, Create, gear, layout switch, chips), its menus or the row controls it draws; a component a column or an action names at size 1 takes the host's size, or none when the host has none. Compact page density then moves them a rung down with the page (32 at 1280); a host with size="1" or "1/2" hands that size down as before.

Over SIMAI Framework ui-a0370c0c99fb (core.runtime 1.49.0; the set still needs 1.43.0 or newer). New relations: dot, tooltip, cl-segmented. Nothing to change for a host that does not use the new settings.

The shadow at the edge of the pinned columns reads the surface role --sf-surface-state-select (the neutral 8% step, light and dark, and the place's own inside a place) instead of the public ramp --sf-alpha-8: over SIMAI Framework ui-7fb26d395af2 no component reads --sf-alpha-* (DEV acceptance 2026-11-10, Q3). Made in ui-pro ahead of simai/ui-view (2026-11-12); the view set releases the same change. Nothing to change for a host.

A row's text starts where the Framework's table now puts it: the published --sf-table--row-text-inset is the cell spacing plus --sf-space-1 (16 at 1440, 12 under compact density and on a phone), the edge inset a list row has, which the table classes give the first cell from utility.table 1.3.0 (ui-source fix/table-classes-g4, C77, C105 H6); it was the cell spacing plus --sf-a8, the 8 every cell had. sf-view-properties pulls a related list out by this number, so the list's row text stays on the field-label axis (with the old number it would stand 8, 4 compact, off it). Needs the SIMAI Framework pair with utility.table 1.3.0; over an older pair a related list stands 8 (4) left of the labels. 1.17.2 is held by another branch. Made in ui-pro ahead of simai/ui-view (2026-11-14); the view set releases the same change. Nothing to change for a host.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use the whole Data View for an admin collection that needs server search, filters, table preferences, actions or pagination.
do_not: Do not rebuild the toolbar, table and pagination from unrelated primitives
Do not let the browser own query or access semantics
Do not send arbitrary field, operator, route or action identifiers to the backend
